Books & audiobooks

Books we recommend

Our go-to reads for understanding your child, from brain science and regulation to autism, ADHD, and PDA. Most are also available as audiobooks.

Alyssa's top pick

Beyond Behaviors

Using Brain Science and Compassion to Understand and Solve Children's Behavioral Challenges

Mona Delahooke, PhD

Explains the brain science behind children's behavior in a way that's easy to follow, and offers a compassionate, relationship-based approach that builds resilience and secure connection.

View on Amazon

Uniquely Human

A Different Way of Seeing Autism

Barry M. Prizant, PhD

Reframes autism through a strengths-based, neurodiversity-affirming lens, helping families understand the reasons behind their child's behaviors.

View on Amazon

Unmasking Autism

Discovering the New Faces of Neurodiversity

Devon Price, PhD

For adults learning about their child or themselves, and for older teens. Covers masking, autistic strengths, common stereotypes, building support, and self-discovery.

View on Amazon

The Way of Play

Using Little Moments of Big Connection to Raise Calm and Confident Kids

Tina Payne Bryson & Georgie Wisen-Vincent

Shows how play supports development, with practical ways for families to play together that build emotional regulation and problem solving.

View on Amazon

The Whole-Brain Child

12 Revolutionary Strategies to Nurture Your Child's Developing Mind

Daniel J. Siegel & Tina Payne Bryson

Explains how emotions and the developing brain work, including how stress can take over the thinking brain, with everyday strategies to help. All of Dan Siegel's books are worth reading.

View on Amazon

Smart but Scattered

The Revolutionary "Executive Skills" Approach to Helping Kids Reach Their Potential

Peg Dawson & Richard Guare

From two ADHD and executive functioning experts, with strategies that build on strengths while supporting harder areas. A teen and adult edition is also available.

View on Amazon

Collaborative Approaches to Learning for Pupils with PDA

Strategies for Education Professionals

Ruth Fidler & Phil Christie

Helps parents and educators support children with PDA (Persistent Drive for Autonomy) at school and in learning.

View on Amazon
